headline: Specialized Access Permits for Sable Island Entry
reservation: Every visitor must receive prior authorization from Parks Canada before landing on the island, whether by air or sea. This is an offshore environment with no commercial accommodations; day trips are the standard. Capacity is strictly limited to protect the wild horse population and sensitive dunes, so verify the registration process well in advance.

days.title: Dunes and Wild Horses
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM landing at the beach airstrip

stops.name: Main Station
stops.detail: Meet with park staff for a safety briefing and to learn about the island's meteorological and research history.

stops.name: West Light
stops.detail: Walk toward the western dunes to observe the iconic Sable Island wild horses and the remnants of historic shipwrecks.

days.driving: Walking only; allow for strenuous movement over soft sand in variable winds.
days.note: Strict distance rules apply when observing horses; do not approach or feed them.

days.title: Atlantic Seals and Marine Life
days.start: Suggested: 8:30 AM from the designated base

stops.name: East Spit
stops.detail: Observe one of the world's largest colonies of grey seals, particularly during the shoulder seasons.

stops.name: Bald Dune
stops.detail: Climb the island's highest point for a 360-degree view of the narrow sandbar and the surrounding Atlantic Ocean.

days.driving: Walking only; distances are deceptive and walking on sand requires significant time.
days.note: Shorelines can change rapidly with the tide; stay clear of the water's edge.

days.title: Flora and Migratory Birds

stops.name: Lily Pond
stops.detail: Discover the rare freshwater ecosystems and endemic plant species that survive in the island's interior.

stops.name: Old Life Saving Station sites
stops.detail: Explore the history of the 'Graveyard of the Atlantic' at various historical markers across the dunes.

days.driving: Walking only; ensure you have coordinated your return flight or boat pick-up time.
days.note: Nesting birds may result in temporary area closures to prevent disturbance.

intel.title: No Vehicles
intel.text: There are no public roads or parking lots on the island. Transport is limited to specialized park vehicles used only by staff for operations.

intel.title: Offshore Connectivity
intel.text: Cellular service is unavailable. The park station has emergency communications, but visitors should not rely on personal mobile devices.

intel.title: No Public Services
intel.text: There are no fuel stations or stores on the island. Visitors must bring all food, water, and necessities for the duration of their stay.

intel.title: Weather Windows
intel.text: Landings are highly dependent on fog and wind conditions. It is common for trips to be delayed or cancelled last minute due to Atlantic weather patterns.

intel.title: Biosecurity Protocols
intel.text: Visitors must scrub footwear to prevent the introduction of invasive species. Access is restricted to designated areas to protect the fragile marram grass.

plan.arrival: Depart from Halifax via chartered fixed-wing aircraft or expedition vessel; ensure all biosecurity checks are completed at the hangar.
plan.vehicle: No rentals available; visitors travel on foot. Ensure footwear is suitable for deep, soft sand and wet conditions.
plan.goldenHour: The South Beach provides expansive views for sunset, though visitors must typically depart before dark per charter schedules.
